subject: Derivative title, training-data & deployment constraints — order form redlines
messages:
From: Evan Park <evan.park@novaprod.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@novaprod.com
Date: Fri, 10 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form redlines (training / output ownership)

Hi Grace / Laura,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached are Novaprod's consolidated redlines to the MSA and the draft Order Form. The two items we flagged as potentially blocking for procurement are:

1) Derivative/assignment language in Section 5 (Output and Productization) — Novaprod's legal team has changed the proposed language to request an assignment of any model derivatives created using customer data.
2) Training & feedback license in Exhibit A — expanded rights to use customer-provided content (including logs & prompts) to train improvements without explicit per-iterate permission.

We'd like to understand Redwood's position on the following practical constraints before we escalate to legal:
- If Redwood agrees to a training license, would we be able to limit it to aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry?
- Can you provide an operational guarantee that model snapshots containing customer prompts will not be used to create a customer-specific model without an additional agreement?

Attaching the redlines and a simple training-data matrix we use for procurement due diligence. If we can resolve the scope and proposed mitigations (telemetry anonymization, opt-out clause, export controls for derivatives), procurement will proceed with a standard C-level approval.

Attached: Novaprod_MSA_redlines_20290810.docx; OrderForm_AnnexA_training_table.xlsx

Thanks,
Evan Park
Head of Legal Operations
Novaprod

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Evan Park <evan.park@novaprod.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2029 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (training / output ownership)

Evan —

Appreciate the clear callouts and the files. Quick internal summary for context: Laura (legal) and Marissa (sales ops) looped in. We're aligned on keeping customer output ownership intact, but the assignment request for derivatives is new and operationally risky for our hosted model roadmap.

High-level proposed responses we can offer without legal escalation: 
- Training/feedback: Redwood is willing to grant a limited "feedback license" for improvements if data is pseudonymized/aggregated and excluded from customer-specific product retraining. We can add an explicit opt-out for training in the Order Form.
- Derivative assignment: we cannot assign model IP. Instead we can offer a scoped license for productization of customer-generated outputs (e.g., if Novaprod builds a product based on the outputs, you get a perpetual, worldwide license to use those outputs) while Redwood retains model derivative IP.

Can you confirm whether Novaprod's procurement would accept: (a) an opt-out training checkbox + telemetry anonymization + audit log evidence; and (b) scoped output license in place of assignment?

If yes, I'll have Laura draft the redline language and circulate back to you. If no, we should escalate to legal to negotiate assignment language and any financial/indemnity tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Contracts, Redwood Inference

--
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Contracts
Redwood Inference
413 555 0198

From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: Evan Park <evan.park@novaprod.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 13 Aug 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (training / output ownership)

Evan —

Thanks for sending the redlines. A few clarifying points from Legal (short bullets so we can move fast):

- Assignment request: our standard position is no assignment of our model derivatives. We are open to narrow carveouts (see below) but assignment would require pricing and SLA concessions.
- Scoped license: Laura proposes the following quick compromise we can redline into the MSA/Order Form: 
  * Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use the Customer Outputs for Customer's internal and commercial purposes ("Outputs License"). 
  * Redwood retains all right, title and interest in model weights, training techniques, and any derivative models trained by Redwood using aggregated telemetry.
  * If Customer requires a customer-specific model (i.e., trained exclusively on Customer data), we will negotiate a separate "Customer Model" addendum with associated fees and export controls.
- Training & Feedback: we will accept a limited feedback license for telemetry if: 
  * Data is pseudonymized and only used in aggregate; 
  * Customer may opt-out via Order Form checkbox; 
  * Redwood will provide a monthly telemetry summary and an audit snapshot on request (subject to standard confidentiality).

Please advise whether these provisions would satisfy Novaprod's procurement/legal team. If they're broadly acceptable, Grace and I will prepare precise redline text and re-upload a tracked-changes doc.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Evan Park <evan.park@novaprod.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: contracts@novaprod.com
Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2029 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines (training / output ownership)

Grace / Laura —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. Procurement has reviewed internally. They can accept the scoped Outputs License in lieu of assignment provided the Order Form includes:

1) The opt-out checkbox for training with clear language that opting out prevents Redwood from using Customer prompts/contents for model improvements that would affect Novaprod's outputs;
2) An obligation for Redwood to provide the monthly telemetry summary + an annual attestation of pseudonymization practices;
3) A procurement-level clause confirming that customer-specific models (if requested later) will be a negotiated addendum with pricing and export-control review.

They asked for redline text for the Order Form checkbox and one paragraph for the MSA clarifying Outputs License vs model derivatives. If you can send tracked redlines by EOD tomorrow, procurement will get this to C-level for signature.

Also copied Novaprod contracts (contracts@novaprod.com) for DocuSign set-up once redlines are agreed.

Appreciate the pragmatism here — will await your tracked doc.

Evan
Head of Legal Operations
Novaprod
